**Short answer:** The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, has been repealed and replaced by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 [S1]. The sources discuss anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, as the earlier law [S3][S4][S5][S6][S7][S8].

**What the sources say:**
* The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, is repealed by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 [S1].
* The Supreme Court noted that "anticipatory bail" means "bail in anticipation of arrest" [S8].
* The Supreme Court stated that an application for anticipatory bail could be made by the accused either "at a stage before an FIR is fi led or at a stage when an FIR is registered but the charge sheet has not been fi led, and the investigation is underway. Alternatively, it can be moved after the completion of investigation" [S8].
**How it may apply:**
* The Supreme Court found no restriction in the text of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, precluding a person from seeking anticipatory bail in relation to an offence while being in custody in relation to another offence [S5].
* The Supreme Court clarified that the option of applying for anticipatory bail while being in custody in relation to a different offence is available "till he is arrested by the police officer on the strength of the P.T. Warrant obtained by him from the court concerned" [S5].

**Uncertain or not covered:** The sources do not state whether the provision for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, has been replaced or what the corresponding provision is under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. To answer definitively, a source detailing the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, regarding anticipatory bail would be needed.

**Jurisdiction and date:** Central law as published on India Code; Supreme Court of India judgments; based on texts retrieved on 2026-09-22.

The text of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is not in the corpus; it was replaced by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, whose section numbers differ.
The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 was repealed from 2024-07-01 and replaced by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

Criminal law changed on 2024-07-01: the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam replaced the Indian Penal Code, the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Indian Evidence Act. Which applies depends on when the events happened and the stage of any proceedings; proceedings pending on that date continue under the old Code.
jurisdiction_note: Central Acts as published on India Code (state amendments only where India Code prints them) and Supreme Court judgments; state rules and later changes may not be covered.
